title: Challenge: recover a lost commit with reflog
intro: Disaster: you ran `git reset --hard HEAD~1` and your last commit, the one with your important work, seems gone. `git log` doesn't show it. Don't panic: Git almost never truly deletes anything. Get it back.

steps.instruction: Look at the reference log, Git's record of every place HEAD has been, to find the lost commit.
steps.success:
d4e5f6a HEAD@{0}: reset: moving to HEAD~1
9a8b7c6 HEAD@{1}: commit: important work   <-- there it is
3c2b1a0 HEAD@{2}: commit: earlier work
steps.fail: There's a command that shows every position HEAD has had, even 'lost' ones.

steps.instruction: The lost commit is 9a8b7c6. Move your branch back to it with a hard reset.
steps.success: HEAD is now at 9a8b7c6 important work, recovered!
steps.fail: Hard-reset your branch onto the recovered commit hash 9a8b7c6.

done: Solved! `git reflog` is your safety net, as long as a commit ever existed, you can almost always bring it back. (If you only wanted that one commit on top of your current work, `git cherry-pick 9a8b7c6` would do it.)
